messages:
incident-bot: Paging @oncall-networking: edge-pop eu-south-az1 experiencing elevated packet loss to upstream peers, latency spike > 300ms, error rate increased > 5%. Alert ID: I-2026-18305. Please acknowledge.
maya: acked. I'm oncall and starting triage. seeing metric spike on edge-pop-eu-south-az1: 20% packet loss to peer ASN 64512 in the last 2m. Loading dashboard now.
maya: quick checks: `dig +short @8.8.8.8 edge.redwood.example.com` looks fine from global checks, but internal healthchecks to edge pop show TCP syn retransmits and short flows failing.
olivia: getting customer reports of streaming stalls and small spike in 503s for eu-south region. No outage yet but degradation for sessions hitting that pop.
maya: running traceroute from our probe -> `traceroute -n 10.20.34.1` shows loss starting at hop 5 (peer switch). `mtr` shows 18-25% pings lost between us and peer.
liam: on way in. possible BGP flap with peering partner? ask netops if there were maintenance windows. @sam can you check peering sessions to ASN 64512 and the router logs for resets?
sam: checking BGP. I see repeated BGP NOTIFICATION from peer at 03:17:22 UTC and session down/up 03:17:22 -> 03:18:05, then flap again 03:20:03 -> 03:20:45. Multiple withdraws for /24s we host at the POP. Looks like peering instability.
maya: that aligns with packetloss windows. Impact: customers routed to this POP hit high latency or timeouts until traffic rebalanced. Likely partial customer impact (10-15% of eu-south requests). Marking severity: Sev2.
liam: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily steer traffic away from eu-south-az1 by updating our POP routing policy (BGP community-based prefer fallback POP), 2) request partner to stabilize peering or move traffic via alternative IX, 3) lower DNS TTL for app hostnames to accelerate client re-resolution if needed.
olivia: +1 on lowering TTL. But note many clients use persistent connections, so BGP steering will be faster for active flows.
sam: applied route policy change to prefer eu-south-az2 for incoming paths from peer AS 64512. Executed: `bgp policy attach pop-steer-eu-south-az2` pushed at 03:26:10 UTC.
maya: confirming metrics: packet loss on az1 down from 22% -> 2% within 90s of policy change, error rate dropped to baseline. Some sessions still failing due to sticky clients.
liam: reached out to partner NOC, they acknowledged a flapped interface on their edge router and are replacing the module. Asked for ETA, they said 20-30m for replacement.
olivia: customers with persistent issues: Customer A (streaming) and Customer B (webhooks). Notifying support to open tickets and patch users with recommended retry/backoff.
maya: handing incident to liam for follow-up and post-incident. I'll do a 15m overlap handoff: summary -> BGP flap to peer ASN 64512 caused withdraws, traffic steered away via BGP policy, partner replacing module, monitoring shows stabilization. @liam take it.
liam: taking over. I'll keep monitoring, confirm partner fix, validate no DNS churn required. If partner doesn't stabilize in 30m we will initiate emergency traffic blackholing for that peer and move to secondary transit.
maya: thanks — switching to standby. Posting brief to #oncall-handoff and will attach these notes.
incident-bot: Incident I-2026-18305 status changed: mitigation in progress (traffic steering applied). Assigned -> liam.
liam: partner NOC reports module swapped at 03:49:12 UTC, BGP flaps stopped. Monitoring shows steady state. Will leave mitigation policy in place for 10m then gradually remove to observe.
sam: removed temporary policy at 03:59:40 UTC (graceful rollback). Confirmed BGP sessions stable for 10m. No further withdraws.
olivia: customers updated: support tickets created for Customer A and B, with notes about transient packet loss and resolution. No billing impact expected.
liam: marking incident as mitigated. We'll run postmortem: items - improve peering monitoring (faster detection of NOTIFICATION messages), consider automatic short-term traffic steering on repeated withdraws, and add runbook step for TTL reduction when appropriate.
maya: closing notes: time to mitigation ~9 minutes from page to initial policy application. Good coordination. I'll draft timeline for postmortem.
incident-bot: Incident I-2026-18305 resolved (mitigated). If further regressions appear, reopen or start new thread.
